correctness.rationale: For n=2s+1, Q=4^s and m=(2Q+1)/3, the regular differential basis satisfies 4i+mj<=2Q-4 with 0<=j<=2. Expansion y=y^Q+sum_{t<s} x^(m4^t) and iterated Q-Cartier residue extraction show only j=1 contributes, at i_t=(Q-4^t-3)/3, producing s linearly independent forms x^(2(4^t-1)/3)dx. j=0 and j=2 residue ranges vanish, and every terminal exponent is even, so C^n=0. This agrees exactly with the older October 25 full proof and its monomial image.
